subject: business-studies
title: Finance Foundations Adventure
welcome_lead: You'll meet revenue, costs and profit — and learn the difference between fixed and variable costs.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies finance foundations — revenue, fixed vs variable costs, gross and net profit.
final_note: You can define revenue, separate fixed from variable costs, and calculate gross and net profit.

concepts.def: Money earned from sales (price x quantity)
Cost that doesn't change with output (e.g. rent)
Cost that rises with output (e.g. materials)
Gross profit minus all other expenses

walkthroughs.body_html:
Revenue = price × quantity sold.

It's the top line on the income statement — money in, before any costs are taken off.

Fixed costs stay the same whatever the output (rent, salaries, insurance).

Variable costs change with output (raw materials, packaging, piece-rate wages). Total cost = fixed + variable.

Gross profit = revenue − cost of sales. It shows how well the core product makes money.

Net profit = gross profit − all other expenses (rent, wages, marketing). The true bottom line.

mcqs.q: Which is a FIXED cost for a bakery?

numericals.q: Revenue £80,000. Cost of sales £30,000. Other expenses £20,000. What is net profit, in £?

free_texts.q: What term describes a cost that does NOT change with output? Two words, second word 'cost'.
